knowledge-base.overview: Shelf 1.x guardrails, Pipeline/Router composition, handler patterns, middleware writing rules, request/response handling, error management, and testing. Applies to Dart REST APIs, microservices, and backend services. A Handler is FutureOr<Response> Function(Request) — keep it functional and thin. Business logic lives in services, not handlers or middleware.

core-principles.principle: Everything flows through Pipeline. Compose handlers with addMiddleware then addHandler. Middleware order is outermost-first.
Handlers receive a Request and return a Response. Parse, delegate to service, serialize, return. No business logic inside handlers.
Use request.change(context: {...}) to pass data downstream between middleware and handlers. Never use mutable globals.
Use Cascade to try handlers in sequence. Specific routes first (API), then generic fallback (static files).
Handlers call services. Services call repositories. No database queries or business rules in middleware or handlers directly.

guardrail.rule: Never let unhandled exceptions propagate to shelf_io.serve. Always wrap the router in error-handling middleware that catches all exceptions and returns structured JSON.
guardrail.bad: // Without error middleware — any uncaught exception crashes the response final handler = const Pipeline().addHandler(router.call);

guardrail.rule: Never call request.readAsString() more than once — the body is a stream and is consumed on the first read. Read once, store the result.
guardrail.bad: final body1 = await request.readAsString(); final body2 = await request.readAsString(); // empty — stream already consumed
guardrail.good: final body = await request.readAsString(); final json = jsonDecode(body) as Map<String, dynamic>;

guardrail.rule: Always load secrets from Platform.environment via a Config class. Never hardcode connection strings, JWT secrets, or API keys.
Set Content-Type: application/json on every response that has a JSON body. Missing Content-Type causes clients to misparse the response.
Keep handler methods under 20 lines. Delegate all business logic to services. A handler that does more than: parse, delegate, serialize is too fat.
Use typed custom exceptions (NotFoundException, ValidationException, UnauthorizedException). Never throw Exception('message') — untyped exceptions cannot be caught specifically.
Use request.change(context: {...request.context, 'key': value}) to pass auth users and other data from middleware to handlers. Never use global variables for request-scoped data.
Wire graceful shutdown via ProcessSignal.sigint.watch(). Call app.close() before server.close() to release database connections cleanly.
Parse query parameters defensively with int.tryParse and a fallback default. Never assume query parameters are present or correctly typed.
Compile to native executable for production deployments. Never run dart run in production — it starts the VM with the Dart SDK overhead.
